production_source_and_binary_identity.assessment: The production code delta in candidate/src/nouveau/tgd3d/tgd3d_dxgi.cpp:120-130 is minimal and semantically correct: args->Reserved == 1 is accepted only when dev->nvk is true and dev->interfaceVersion == D3DWDDM2_0_DDI_INTERFACE_VERSION (0x000b0020); Reserved == 0 remains unchanged; Reserved >= 2 or Reserved == 1 on non-NVK/non-WDDM2.0 paths returns E_INVALIDARG before touching Device/Resource state or forwarding. Present1 is wired to both DXGI1_3 (tgd3d_dxgi.cpp:368) and DXGI1_4 (tgd3d_dxgi.cpp:387, filled on WDDM 2.0 in tgd3d_device.cpp:316). Global GetSupportedVersions (tgd3d_entry.cpp:40-45) continues not to advertise WDDM 2.0 by default. Device/Resource ownership checks (tgd3d_dxgi.cpp:133,32), SubResourceIndex bounds, Flags.Reserved rejection (tgd3d_dxgi.cpp:41), flush/device-loss handling, and Present(&present) return propagation remain intact. Frozen binary/signing artifacts report PE section equivalence (.buildid-only diff) against both rebuilt baseline b4f6c7bf and prior process-scoped candidate 4d35f14b, matching export table (OpenAdapter/OpenAdapter10/OpenAdapter10_2), and local CA Authenticode verification exit 0 for signed ARM64 DLL dcc71e34e229c7090d05b424e03ef959b682170eb8fed7e2c77684d041426688; however, source-identity.json is stale relative to canonical source commit 329d0d21a96f0dc2958b954723fc2984c07b4613 (Finding F6).

No C++ test execution receipt exists in evidence/, confirming the ported test suite was not run against the candidate source.

policy_and_release_gate.assessment: Existing closure-based verified-fix rules, closed-fault 3-run requirements, and existing open-faults.json / graphics-baseline.json records remain compatible, and host test receipts show 63/63 PowerShell unit checks and 2/2 isolated Git publication checks passed. However, static review identified reachable gate gaps in the new scoped verified-fix path: (1) scope-mixing bypass if paired with baseline_comparisons (F2), (2) missing open-status enforcement and missing case-vs-proof hash distinctness check (F3), (3) unconditional output_verified=true requirement conflicting with the user-specified empty-window Reserved=1 test (F4), (4) lack of fault.verified_fix ledger validation and post-supersession evidence retention (F5), and (5) hash casing inconsistency (F7). Native-Boot.ps1 and Baseline-Device.ps1 integrate cleanly with Assert-SwitchPromotion and Assert-SwitchCaseFiles once the updated policy snapshot and supporting evidence files are staged alongside qualification.json.

existing_native_evidence.assessment: Retained process-scoped control proves baseline Reserved=1 -> Present1 E_INVALIDARG (0x80070057) -> DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED (0x887a0005 / reason 0x887a0020) on both Sequential and FlipSequential, while the process-scoped candidate passed FlipSequential native-modern-empty (S_OK, no display samples) and native-modern-clear (S_OK, 5/5 desktop samples) but hit an unexplained Kernel-Power 41 / EventLog 6008 restart during the 6-frame native-modern-full trial after 2 successful Presents and entry into the 3rd Present (trace ended 8.643 ms before entry; cause remains open).

findings.summary: Ported runtime_contracts.cpp contains a dirty-rectangle bounds assertion that unconditionally fails against candidate tgd3d_dxgi.cpp, and no passing C++ test run is recorded in evidence/.
findings.reachable_scenario: Compiling and running runtime_contracts() (specifically presentation13_contracts()) against the frozen candidate tree. After setting dirty[1].right = 66 on a 65x17 surface, dxgi.pfnPresent1(&present) does not inspect DirtyRects/pDirtyRects, forwards to Present(&present), pushes 4 into presentOrder, and returns DXGI_STATUS_OCCLUDED instead of E_INVALIDARG, triggering CHECK failure and std::exit(1).
findings.impact: The C++ unit test file bundled in canonical source commit 329d0d21a96f0dc2958b954723fc2984c07b4613 is broken against the shipped Present1 implementation, and the four ported Reserved-word regression checks (lines 794-809) have no verified execution on this candidate tree.
findings.minimal_fix: Update candidate/src/nouveau/tgd3d/tests/runtime_contracts.cpp:812-813 to align with the deployed Present1 contract (dirty rectangles are optional hints forwarded via pDXGIContext and not bounds-rejected in Present1; test an enforced Present1 guard such as SubResourceIndex >= res->subresources() or null phSurfacesToPresent instead), also assert dxgi14.pfnPresent1 == dxgi.pfnPresent1 (or test WDDM 2.0 Reserved=1 through dxgi14.pfnPresent1), then build and execute runtime_contracts and archive its passing log in evidence/.

findings.summary: A scoped verified-fix paired with a baseline_comparisons entry bypasses independent_qualifications, per-fault assessments, and distinct working-path control verification.
findings.reachable_scenario: A qualification with change_kind='verified-fix' and verified_fix.scope (which has no control_sha256) is referenced in open-faults.json under baseline_comparisons instead of independent_qualifications during Select, Check, Publish, CheckPublication, or Native-Boot -Mode Accept. Assert-SwitchVerifiedFix succeeds on lines 149-184; Assert-SwitchPromotion enters if ($comparison.Count) at line 293, takes the else branch at line 304, compares $working[0].evidence_sha256 against $null ($Evidence.verified_fix.control_sha256) at line 308 (always false), and returns at line 314 without checking independent_qualifications or fault_assessments.
findings.impact: Allows promoting a scoped repair while skipping per-fault accounting for all other open faults and without requiring a candidate working-path control or distinctness from previous_control_sha256.
findings.minimal_fix: In Baseline-Promotion.ps1:294 (or inside the else block at line 304), explicitly reject scoped verified-fix qualifications in baseline_comparisons: `if ($Evidence.change_kind -ceq 'verified-fix' -and $Evidence.verified_fix.PSObject.Properties['scope']) { throw 'Scoped repair must account for open faults via independent_qualifications' }`, and add a negative test in Test-BaselinePromotion.ps1.

findings.summary: Scoped verified-fix validation does not require the target fault to remain status='open', and does not ensure case_sha256 is distinct from the three supporting proof hashes.
findings.reachable_scenario: (1) During Assert-SwitchVerifiedFix, if a closed fault still carries a historical verified_fix object, line 150 (`Where-Object id -CEQ $binding.fault_id`) matches it without checking `$_.status -ceq 'open'`. (2) If a qualification sets verified_fix.case_sha256 equal to causal_evidence_sha256, code_review_sha256, or build_sha256, lines 169-171 only check pairwise uniqueness among the 3 proof hashes and accept the collision.
findings.impact: (1) Allows mixing scoped open-fault repair rules onto a closed fault; (2) allows reusing a static cause/review/build proof file as the native candidate boot test receipt.
findings.minimal_fix: At Baseline-Promotion.ps1:150, require open status: `$matches = @($Ledger.faults | Where-Object { $_.id -ceq $binding.fault_id -and $_.status -ceq 'open' })`. At lines 172-173, enforce distinctness of case_sha256 from the 3 proof hashes: `if ($binding.case_sha256 -in $proofHashes) { throw 'Scoped repair native case must be distinct from cause, review and build evidence' }`. Add negative tests in Test-BaselinePromotion.ps1.

findings.summary: Assert-SwitchPromotion unconditionally requires output_verified=true on every case for change_kind='verified-fix', conflicting with the user-specified empty-window Reserved=1 verification.
findings.reachable_scenario: When qualifying the actual production package using only the user-specified empty-window Reserved=1 test (matching native-modern-empty in wddm20-present1-native-window.json:143,173,183 where display_samples=null and on_screen_observation=null), Assert-SwitchPromotion line 281 rejects the qualification unless the empty-window case sets output_verified=true.
findings.impact: Forces either claiming output_verified=true on an empty-window test that only verifies Present1 callback forwarding/S_OK return (as happened in test_baseline_publication.py:190,196) or adding unrequested rendering cases (and even with an extra case, line 280 iterates over every case in $Evidence.cases, so the empty-window case still cannot truthfully set output_verified=false).
findings.minimal_fix: Keep output_verified=true mandatory for presentation and closure-based verified-fix qualifications, while for scoped verified-fix (`$Evidence.change_kind -ceq 'verified-fix' -and $Evidence.verified_fix.PSObject.Properties['scope']`) require normal_exit=true and desktop_available=true on every case and make output_verified=true required only when the registered fault.verified_fix requires visible-output verification (or when a non-empty visual scenario is registered).

findings.summary: fault.verified_fix is not validated by Assert-SwitchFaultLedger/CheckLedger, its review/build proof files lose pre-push retention once a later baseline supersedes graphics-baseline.json, and check_graphics_baseline_push.py does not guard against verified_fix: null.
findings.reachable_scenario: (1) Committing a malformed fault.verified_fix in open-faults.json passes CheckLedger until Select. (2) After a future baseline replaces graphics-baseline.json, retained_reports() (check_graphics_baseline_push.py:156-161) only inspects the currently selected qualification, and lines 172-177 only retain fault.evidence and closed fault.resolution files; modifying or deleting the earlier scoped repair's review or build proof files is no longer caught by pre-push or CheckLedger. (3) If a qualification contains '"verified_fix": null', check_graphics_baseline_push.py:160 raises AttributeError, which is not caught by the except clause on line 243.
findings.impact: Malformed scoped-repair registrations can enter open-faults.json unchecked; retained independent-review and signed-build proofs for an open scoped repair are not tamper-protected across subsequent baseline promotions the way closed-fault proofs are.
findings.minimal_fix: Validate fault.verified_fix schema/hashes/commit/components in Assert-SwitchFaultLedger whenever present on an open fault (and forbid it or check consistency on closed faults); record repository-relative causal_evidence_file, code_review_file, and build_file on fault.verified_fix and verify/retain them in Select-GraphicsBaseline.ps1:66-85 and check_graphics_baseline_push.py:172-177; guard check_graphics_baseline_push.py:160 with `(data.get('verified_fix') or {}).get('evidence') or []`.

findings.summary: Scoped verified-fix uses case-sensitive SHA-256 comparisons (-cne/-CEQ) while Assert-SwitchHash and all other profile/case hash checks are case-insensitive.
findings.reachable_scenario: On-device Windows PowerShell collection writes uppercase Get-FileHash output into loaded_components or evidence_sha256 while components uses lowercase hex.
findings.impact: Causes spurious rejection during Select/Check/Native-Boot on valid uppercase-hex SHA-256 values (no security bypass).
findings.minimal_fix: Either enforce canonical lowercase hex in Assert-SwitchHash (`-cnotmatch '^[0-9a-f]{64}$'`) or use case-insensitive `-ne`/`-eq` for SHA-256 comparisons at lines 164, 165, 173, and 181.
